clue.text: Cause of unexpected fall perhaps in British people eating pineapple

indicators.note: the British people take the fruit inside them, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: your kin are your family, your people
ananas is the French (and botanical) name for the pineapple

explanation.surface: A comic image of British people tucking into a pineapple, with a pratfall promised.
explanation.walkthrough: Ananas, the pineapple's name in much of Europe, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipping on discarded fruit peel is the classic slapstick tumble, hence 'perhaps' marking an example.

clue.text: Steals lots

definitions.meaning: to bag something is to pinch or steal it

explanation.surface: A terse note on theft on a grand scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Bag is slang for taking illicitly, and 'bags of' is a colloquial plenty.

clue.text: Country of one billion and rising, Amnesty International fellow to tour

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the reversed charity-and-fellow goes around the other piece
in a down entry rising means the letters read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: AI is the abbreviation of the human-rights charity
a fellow is a man
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A human-rights charity worker setting off round a nation of a billion people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' sits beside 'one billion' but reverses the charity and fellow (AIMAN backwards); 'to tour' has that go round the one-billion letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is a nation in south-west Africa.

clue.text: Student's introduced to excited masses with iconic type of art

indicators.note: the student is brought into the middle of the jumbled letters
excited letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: L, the learner plate, stands for a student; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A student is presented to an enthusiastic crowd alongside some celebrated work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' shuffles the twelve letters; 'introduced to' places the learner's L among them. 'type of art' is the definition, not part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoclassicism is an eighteenth-century movement in painting and architecture reviving Greek and Roman models.

clue.text: Army promoted banks of irregulars to guard monarch

parts.note: to promote an idea is to sell it, so promoted gives sold

indicators.note: the outer letters stand either side of the monarch, protecting it
the banks of a river are its edges, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A rebel army advances its irregular flanks to protect the king.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is made up of soldiers, the plural standing for the force.

clue.text: Suffer, having no interest to wipe out debts

indicators.note: the debts are cancelled, struck out of the longer word

parts.note: incurious means lacking curiosity or interest
IOUs are written promises of debts

explanation.surface: Someone who suffers, uninterested, hoping their debts will be cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no interest' looks financial, beside 'debts', but means lack of curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to suffer or bring it on oneself.

clue.text: Active agent must possess core element of secrecy

indicators.note: the agent holds the central letter inside

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy

indicators.note: the core is the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A field agent must keep secrecy at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone lively and nimble, especially in older age.

clue.text: Pick youngster for sports team magazine

parts.note: to play someone for a sports team is to pick them
a boy is a youngster

explanation.surface: A selector picks a young lad for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: PLAY means 'pick for sports team', its phrase split by 'youngster'.
explanation.definitionFit: Playboy is the long-running American men's monthly founded by Hugh Hefner.

clue.text: After variable years, Ted's transformed in recent past

indicators.note: the anagram comes after the variable

parts.note: x, y and z are variables in algebra

indicators.note: transformed letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Ted has changed greatly over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' shuffles YEARS and TEDS into ESTERDAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterdays are bygone days, the not-so-distant times gone by.

clue.text: Soup beginning to inflame large mouth ulcer

parts.note: gumbo is a thick Louisiana soup-stew

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Hot soup starting to inflame a big ulcer in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumboil is an abscess on the gum, a sore in the mouth.

clue.text: Something providing direction and order during Conservative predicament

indicators.note: the order sits within the other pieces

parts.note: a pretty pass is a difficult situation
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Political commentary: the Tories need direction and discipline in their crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass points to north, giving a traveller bearings.

clue.text: Sources of tremendous influence within America list novel as obsessively consumerist

indicators.note: the two first letters go inside the anagram
novel means new, signalling a fresh arrangement
the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A commentator says a novel list holds huge influence over American culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but is the anagram signal; 'within' puts the two initials inside the shuffled letters, just before the final C.
explanation.definitionFit: Materialism is the excessive attachment to possessions and buying things.

clue.text: In America, check Iowa road index for place pots are made

parts.note: Americans call a restaurant bill a check
IA is the postal code for Iowa
an index can be a table of figures

explanation.surface: A US traveller checks a road index for Iowa to find a pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pots' suggests ceramics; in snooker or billiards a pot sends a ball into a pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Shots that pocket balls happen on the baize surface of the cue-sports table.

clue.text: Outdoor garment husband wears at concert that rocks

indicators.note: the husband is inside, as if wearing the rest
rocks means shakes about, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: H is the genealogical abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband dresses for a lively rock concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' suggests music but signals the shuffle; 'wears' has the H inside it, as if the husband had the garment on.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench coat is a belted military-style raincoat worn outside.

clue.text: Brace of flightless birds, fast but not hot

indicators.note: the hot letter is left out of the birds

parts.note: rheas are large South American flightless birds
H abbreviates hot, as on a tap
fast can mean firm or secure, i.e. sure

explanation.surface: A pair of flightless birds run fast, but not in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brace' tempts as 'a pair' of birds, but it is a verb, to bolster.
explanation.definitionFit: To brace someone is to steady or fortify them, as reassurance does.

clue.text: Hoped indeed to split power with Republican and Democrat

indicators.note: the word for indeed goes between the letters, separating them

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
aye means yes, indeed

explanation.surface: Someone hopes the parties will genuinely share power in Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: To pray for something is to wish or hope earnestly for it.

clue.text: Offended salesman shouted, losing equanimity finally

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: the final letter is taken out of the shouted word

parts.note: yelled means shouted

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: An angry salesman loses his cool and yells.
explanation.definitionFit: Repelled can mean disgusted or put off, i.e. offended.

clue.text: Fool with money backing idiot's tips

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the money word reads right to left

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

indicators.note: the tips are the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A fool backs an idiot's betting tips with money.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a silly, foolish person.

clue.text: Proposition nothing to do with article male pens

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in, so the outer pieces enclose the others

parts.note: the is the definite article
O looks like zero, nothing
re means concerning, to do with

explanation.surface: A man writes a proposal that has nothing to do with the article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like writing but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a theorem is a proposition to be proved.

clue.text: Genealogical study led Harry all over the place

indicators.note: scattered everywhere, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Prince Harry leading a chaotic family-history project.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldry studies coats of arms and the lineage of families who bear them.

clue.text: PC Plod takes heed when turning up at intervals

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up reverses the letters
only every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A police constable called Plod pays attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' looks like a police constable but means a computer. Every other letter gives POTKSED, which 'turning up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A desktop is a personal computer designed for a desk.

clue.text: Flowering shrub of Great Britain, said to cause irritation

indicators.note: said tells us the answer is how the words sound when spoken

parts.note: hebe is a flowering evergreen shrub and GB is Great Britain, so a hebe of GB's is a 'hebe GB's'

explanation.surface: A British garden shrub reputedly brings on a rash.
explanation.definitionFit: The heebie-jeebies are a state of jittery nerves or unease.

clue.text: Press union over cheers for unelected military government

indicators.note: over means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: the NUJ is the National Union of Journalists
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: The journalists' union applauds a military takeover.
explanation.definitionFit: A junta is a group of officers ruling after seizing power.

clue.text: Begs son to pursue job after wasting time

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so the son goes after
wasting time means the time letter is dropped

parts.note: a task is a job

explanation.surface: A parent begging their son to go after a job after time-wasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask is to request or beg for something.

clue.text: How a dry summer regularly attracts northern chaps catching crabs?

indicators.note: the summer letters draw in the northern letter, adding it on
regularly means taking letters at even intervals

explanation.surface: Wondering how a dry summer could draw in Northern men with a crab problem.
explanation.walkthrough: Catching a crab is a rower's error, the oar stuck in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers are the men who can 'catch a crab' with a misplaced oar stroke.

clue.text: Untidy toilets? That's some understatement!

indicators.note: untidy letters are in disorder

explanation.surface: Someone shrugging that dirty toilets are hardly a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the rhetorical figure of understatement, e.g. 'not bad'.

clue.text: Dull morning following temperature close to heatwave

indicators.note: the morning comes after the temperature

parts.note: a.m. means morning

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A dull morning after a hot spell nears its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tame means unexciting, insipid.

clue.text: Pictures of ordinary ducks without any crests

indicators.note: each word loses its crest, its top or first letter

parts.note: bland means ordinary, unremarkable
to duck something is to escape it

explanation.surface: Pictures of everyday ducks lacking head plumage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' are birds in the surface but a verb, escapes, in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Landscapes are paintings of rural scenery.
